Class WindowEngine

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.window.WindowEngine
public final class WindowEngine extends Object
The resolution engine of THE ONE WINDOW — MK ring-0, pure policy, no Minecraft I/O. Every behavior of every addressable thing flows through one method: resolve(Address, BehaviorKey). The engine never branches on KindTag; it sorts Decls by the frozen cascade and returns a fully-resolved value, always non-null.

The frozen two-axis cascade

  1. AXIS 1 — authority (higher): server-tier authoritative declaration > client-tier declaration > library default. Compared only where a key's Tier makes it meaningful. Plugs in at Phase 3b via the server-tier port; this client engine holds only client-tier decls.
  2. AXIS 2 — specificity (within equal authority): per-slot override > per-group default > library default.
  3. Tie-break: last-declared wins (here: the last registered matching group).
A Decl.Set stops the walk with its value; Decl.Inherit or the absence of a declaration falls through; the walk always terminates at the key's BehaviorKey.libraryDefault() (the Null-Object bottom). So a slot nobody touched resolves straight to the vanilla-equivalent default.

This client store is MK-resident and MK-alone usable. The server tier (the MKC BehaviorBindingTable feeding AXIS-1) arrives in Phase 3b/3c.

Threading

Declaration (set/setGroup) and resolution (resolve) are expected on the client thread (declare at screen/menu setup, resolve during render/input). The store is nonetheless safe under incidental cross-thread access: the maps are concurrent, GROUPS is copy-on-write, group creation is serialized in bindingFor(GroupKey), and every Decl is immutable — so a resolve racing a declaration sees a consistent old-or-new value, never torn state. (The Phase-3b server port supplies AXIS-1 declarations through the same immutable-Decl contract.)
